messages.text: just pushed migration 001 and 002. i added a graph_version trigger so we can invalidate the alias cache when the ontology changes. do you want to own the mv for idf?
yes i'll do that. just finished the dockerfile btw, it builds clean now
nice. wait, did you use uuids for the concept id? i was planning bigints for speed
uuids. they're everywhere in the api already and it makes joins simpler if we ever sharding. bigint is faster but not by much for this scale
fine, uuids win. i'll just update my local schema to match. annoying that i have to change the join logic in the resolver
honestly it's fine. also i just pushed 003 and 004. you might want to pull, they handle the relation table indexes
wait, i already have a 003 and 004 locally. collision. mine are for the user_interests table
oh no. sorry. let me rename mine to 005 and 006 and push again. you keep 003/004?
yeah keep mine. it's cleaner if we just number sequentially from now on. i'll rename my 001/002 to 000_init and 000b so there's no ambiguity
done. pushed 005 and 006. now the numbering makes sense (ish)
perfect. i'm going to start coding the exact alias match stage now. should be quick since it's just a lookup
cool. let me know if you need any new indexes for that
probably not, the primary key on concept_id should be enough. i'll add a unique constraint on the alias string too
smart. good night john, for real this time
